line: Broad shoulders like yours bend standard border-plate; step by the anvil when you want real rivets.
You carry that shield like you actually take blows on it, lass. Most greenhorns drop theirs by the ford.
Keep your bowstrings greased against this fen-damp; wet hemp snaps loud enough to wake every gnoll.
Steady eyes on you, archer. Watch the chalk ridge—quill-fiends love trading shots with scouts.
Mind your sparks near my drying shelves, scholar; one stray ember turns dried marsh-rue into poison smoke.
A hedge-witch with clean cuffs? Rare sight in Thornwick. Bring me kiln-glass if you value good mana draughts.
Keep your bone-charms tucked under your coat in the chapel yard; the widows here have buried enough kin.
You smell of grave-loam and cold tallow, woman. Use your dark craft on the bog-dead, not our churchyard.
Scrape that Ravenwatch mud off your greaves before you sit—my floorboards took three winters to season.
Goose-fletched quarrels just arrived from Ashbrook; buy them now before Garrick's quartermaster claims the lot.
Keep your staff-light hooded on my punt; bog-wisps swarm glowing crystal like moths to tallow.
If one of your pale thralls steps onto my cargo plank, I'm pushing both of you into the weir.
Spider-ichor pits cheap iron overnight; bring your blade here so I can burn the venom off the edge.
Word is your arrows pinned the Silk Widow before her third clutch hatched. First mug at the tavern is mine.
The ossuary wards stopped humming the hour Morvessa fell. You burned through silk older than the border.
Even I must admit it—turning the ossuary's own dead against that spider saved fifty border spears.
Captain Garrick paid his tab in fresh Mint silver this morning. Seems you're an honest man after all.
Private caravan guards are bragging about cheap ash-shaft bolts today. Funny how supply wagons go light.
Never saw lightning crack a shield-wall like you did at Alder Bridge, master wizard. Glad you're on our payroll.
You don't buy much steel, pale lady, yet your bone-guards soak more arrows than my best tower shields.
Oil your plate twice a day in Redmarsh, soldier; alkali dust eats through leather straps by sundown.
Hope you brought linen under-padding, vanguard; sun-baked steel blisters shoulders faster than firepots.
Account for cross-winds off the salt-pans, bowman—gusts here push an arrow three paces wide at fifty yards.
Good call wrapping your bow-limbs in rawhide, sister. Dry basin heat splits unbacked ash wood clean.
Feel that static in your fingertips? The wardstones here bleed raw lightning into any open spell-weave.
Keep your focus crystal grounded when dust storms roll in, mage—dry grit sparks like flint.
At least those dry-bone servants of yours don't drink half my cistern before noon. More water for paying men.
Keep your shade-hounds away from my sweet-water casks, death-speaker; cold air turns my brine-seals brittle.
Highgate's palisade would be charcoal if your shield-line hadn't held the breach against those firepots.
Picked twenty curved sand-raider arrows out of my wagon bed—take them if you don't mind desert fletching.
My ears are still ringing from that wardstone rupture. Whatever counter-sigil you cast kept the camp standing.
Seeing our dead kin rise with picks to batter their own overseers... grim work, stranger, yet fair.
Those femur-flutes you brought me sing in pre-dynastic wind-modes! Every step across the flats feels lighter.
Three centuries of acoustic ward-craft smashed to gravel because a soldier couldn't bear eerie whistling.
Caravans are rolling through the central basin without losing a single mule since you felled the Sand Glutton.
Scouts found a forty-foot sinkhole where Gorrathul collapsed. You put enough shafts in him to fence a paddock.
The unnatural chill over the southern dunes vanished when that belly-maw closed forever. Brilliant work.
Even the desert worms won't touch Gorrathul's carcass after the rot-curses you wove into its hide.
Tomas's freed quarrymen forged half a ton of new spear-tips this week—all because you held that gallery.
After the Fork of Spears, nobody in Redmarsh questions an outlander's aim. Drink on the house today.
Keep off the wet gangplanks in full plate, man—Oakhaven's harbor mud swallows armored knights whole.
Salt spray rusts border steel in a single watch; rub whale-tallow into your pauldrons before boarding.
Sea-fog bends light across the mudflats, archer—aim a hand's breadth low when shooting over surf.
We need sharp eyes on the seawall turrets; Kael's skiffs slip right under the mist at flood tide.
If you can boil water with a finger-snap, my triage tents need three cauldrons heated before sundown.
A disciplined arcanist is worth ten surgeons when gangrene spreads through the lower ward.
You look right at home in Oakhaven's fog, guv—half our drowned sailors walk the flats at low tide anyway.
Keep your cold fingers off my salvage crates, pale miss—I found those barnacle-chests fair and square.
Holding Sundered Ranks against privateer boarding-pikes bought our shipwrights two whole days to caulk hulls.
Salvaged barbed harpoon-heads from the Sunken Citadel—heavy draw, yet they punch straight through crab-shell.
Cooling those cinder-wards saved half the cliffside barracks from blistering heat-fever.
Your tireless bone-hands hauled twice as much oak timber at Riverlock as my dock-gangs could lift.
Kael's gunners fired blind into the fog all morning—burning those cipher tables saved our north pier.
Salted herring in every pot tonight! When Kael's fire-ships come, every dockhand grabs a water-bucket for you.
Hope privateer gold keeps your robes warm, lady—our kids are chewing boiled kelp while you count coins.
That cursed bone-organ stopped echoing across the bay at last. My carpenters can finally hear their hammers.
The southern channel cleared of spectral fog the moment Vesperion's choir fell silent. We can sail at dawn.
My apprentices stopped waking with nosebleeds the hour you shattered that six-winged prelate.
Unbinding an arch-prelate's choir takes iron will, necromancer. Even the drowned dead rest quieter tonight.
You walked through burning pitch on the harbor piers and still came back for stout. Drink free till we sail.
Caldera heat warps cheap mail into tin; let me quench your breastplate in prism-dust before you march.
Good heavy steel on you, shield-sister, though volcanic ash will chew those leather joints in two watches.
Thermal updrafts above the fissures lift light arrows straight into the soot—use heavy bodkin points.
Keep smoked glass handy on the ridge, archer; sulfur flares blind an unshielded eye in half a breath.
Speak your incantations cleanly near the obsidian pillars; the caldera echoes hungry names back at casters.
Frost magic is worth its weight in sovereign gold down here, magister—keep your cold wards primed.
Hundreds of First-Watch wardens burned to ash on these steps. Tread lightly before calling on old bones.
Neither ash nor magma scares you, death-weaver. Just keep your spirits bound when we reach the Threshold.
Greystone's east wall still stands because you held the breach while demonic catapults hammered the glacis.
Picking off those ash-weavers on the beacon crags kept my powder-kegs from going up early.
Malrik's shadow-constructs melted like wax against your counter-spells. The gorge supply line is open.
Singing iron cliffs tugged my breastplate sideways in the Gauntlet, yet your bone-men marched straight through.
With those copper spikes bleeding off the canyon's pull, my crossbowmen are landing bolts at two hundred paces.
Shame about those two sappers' legs, yet the raw magnetic ore you shook loose will plate twenty shields.
Breaking the Three-Roads siege united our vanguard; nothing stands between Ironcamp and the Threshold now.
The Anchor Seals hum in harmony with your wards, magister. The obsidian doors will yield when you give the word.
The caldera vents cooled three degrees the instant the Cinder King fell. Every anvil in Ironcamp salutes you.
Clear sky above the rim for the first time in a century—and they say your final shaft split his sword-halo.
You froze the Cinder King's throne mid-eruption, magister. Poets will argue over how one mortal held that fire.
The First Watch has laid down its obsidian spears at last. You gave the dead of Thornvael their final peace.
Heavy broadswords eat whetstones fast in wet weather—buy two bars of grey grit while my pack is open.
Warm mutton broth by the hearth, huntress—steady hands don't come from shivering on cold watchtowers.
Stand amidships when we pole across the Sunken Ford, shield-maid; heavy mail tilts a flat-bottomed punt.
I sell marsh-rue salve for living skin, friend—if your bone-servants rot, you'll have to patch them yourself.
Two coppers a ladle for sweet cistern water, iron-clad—and double if your horse drinks from the bucket.
Never saw an arrow thread a slave-pen padlock at forty paces until you cleared the third quarry terrace.
Nothing scatters sand-raider outriders faster than dropping a frost nova right under their lead mules.
Garrison rations are tight at Crossroads, so I won't complain that your silent vanguard eats nothing at all.
Dropped your silver in the harbor silt? Give me a copper and I'll dive under the pilings before tide turns.
Whatever lightning you called down on that Elder Juggernaut cracked coastal bedrock half a league away.
Clean bow-shots save bandage linen—half the raiders you dropped at the manor never even drew steel.
The harbor smells of charred tar and cold salt, yet my taproom stays open as long as you keep Kael's dead down.
Stand in front of my demolition crew when the slag-fiends rush, big man, and I'll blast every gate wide.
Brought in a batch of obsidian-tipped shafts from the landing coves—they'll punch right through demon scale.
The air around West Crag stopped tasting like burnt copper the moment you unmade those capacitor prisms.
I don't care what chapel-priests say about your craft—turning Malrik's own constructs to dust won us the gorge.
Dented shields tell an honest story, veteran. Keep your chin tucked when the heavy mauls swing.
Fresh bow-wax and sinew-cord in stock—a snapped string in the middle of a charge ruins everybody's day.
Old empire ward-craft runs deeper than tavern tales admit; keep detailed notes on every seal you break.
Walk your cold path if you must, sister, so long as every bound soul is released when the ash settles.
